comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C142-C144 regarding main findings and implications for future shrubification. Both evaluations find these conclusions well-supported by the evidence, with OpenEval noting appropriate caution in the extrapolation and peer reviewers accepting the implications for paleoecology and future warming scenarios.

Strong alignment on the new sedaDNA record documentation (C18-C26, C145-C150). Both find the methods and data solid. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of chronology, DNA preservation, and internal consistency. Peer reviewers note minor suggestions for polishing methods and visualization but affirm the fundamental validity of the data.

Strong agreement on the revised Torfdalsvatn chronology and multi-proxy comparison (C31-C43). Both evaluations support the revised age model, the interpretation of early pollen as long-distance transport, and the delayed local colonization shown by sedaDNA and macrofossils. Peer reviewers specifically note the revised version is 'more convincing.'

Good alignment on dispersal mechanism analysis (C127-C136). Both evaluations accept the logic connecting genetic sources, sea ice history, and dispersal mechanisms. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of the reasoning for each location, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the improved discussion without challenge.

Strong agreement on mechanistic explanations for colonization patterns (C102-C104, C110-C116, C121). Both evaluations find the discussion of temperature tolerances, reproductive strategies, and integrated mechanisms well-supported. Peer reviewers note the improved clarity of discussion and accept the identification of drivers.

Strong alignment on synthesis of colonization patterns across sites (C91-C95, C101). Both evaluations accept the patterns showing variable Salicaceae timing, consistent Betulaceae delays, and distance-from-refugia effects. Peer reviewers emphasize the broader implications for deglaciation history across multiple regions.

Good agreement on Icelandic colonization patterns (C44-C48). Both evaluations support the comparison between sites showing similar Betulaceae delays despite different deglaciation times. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of the ~1700 year establishment requirement, while peer reviewers accept this as a key finding without challenge.

Partial overlap on colonization timing interpretations (C52-C53). Both evaluations support these claims about establishment requirements and catchment conditions. OpenEval groups these with broader Icelandic synthesis (R3), while peer reviewers group them separately, but both find the interpretations convincing.

Good alignment on genetic data synthesis (C122-C126, C131). Both evaluations accept the compilation of published genetic origins data. OpenEval integrates this with paleoceanographic evidence for dispersal mechanism analysis, while peer reviewers accept it as supporting context for colonization patterns.

Agreement on modern analog evidence (C117-C120). Both evaluations accept these supporting observations from contemporary systems. OpenEval includes them as part of comprehensive mechanistic explanation, while peer reviewers note them as part of the improved discussion without specific challenge.

Partial overlap on woody shrub colonization timing at new site (C151-C153). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval groups them with broader site documentation, while peer reviewers highlight them separately as central to the manuscript's findings about colonization patterns.

OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of the systematic compilation of published sedaDNA records (C55-C90), noting appropriate citations and interpretive decisions. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers generally accept the comparative approach across multiple sites.

OpenEval evaluates the scientific context and motivation (C1-C7) regarding Arctic warming, shrubification, and model uncertainties. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focus on primary results rather than background framing.

OpenEval evaluates the methodological rationale for using sedaDNA (C8-C15), including limitations of traditional proxies and advantages of sedaDNA for detecting local colonization. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this methodological foundation underlies the accepted results.
